subject: Proposal: 2yr prepay with weighted true‑up and deferred savings path
messages:
From: Elena Gonzalez <elena.gonzalez@elarahealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: 2yr prepay structure ideas

Camila —

Thanks for taking the time last week. We talked internally about moving to a two‑year prepaid arrangement to lock in pricing and simplify billing. A couple of things that are important for us: frontloading some credits in year 1 to cover ramp, a predictable stepdown in unit price in year 2, and a quarterly true‑up (we have seasonal volume spikes).

Can you sketch what that would look like from Redwood’s side? Also need a rough delta to list price and any contract-level commitments you’d expect.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Procurement
Elara Health

Attachment: none

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gonzalez <elena.gonzalez@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Mike Daniels <mike@elarahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: 2yr prepay structure ideas

Elena / Mike —

Appreciate the clarity. I pulled together a starter commercial that should map to your asks. High level: 2yr commitment (annualized $1.2M ARR baseline), 30% of year‑1 committed value due up front (applied as credits to consumption), year‑2 unit price steps down by a negotiated escalator (we propose 12% effective discount vs list in year‑2), and quarterly true‑ups to reconcile actual usage against the committed buckets. We can include a seasonal floor so you’re not over‑charged during expected spikes.

I attached a redlined proposal that shows the math and an accompanying finance model. Key open items for negotiation: the stepdown bands, the true‑up cadence (quarterly vs monthly), and whether you want a partial refund or credit mechanism on true‑up shortfalls.

Next steps: if this maps, I’ll run it through finance for margin check and get a conditional approval from my manager for an up‑front discount band. Also looping legal once we land mechanics.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Elara_Redlined_Proposal_v2.pdf (PDF), finance_margin_model.xlsx (XLSX)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposal: 2yr prepay with weighted true‑up and deferred savings path

Camila —

Thanks for sending the draft. Quick finance read: the headline structure looks feasible but the economics depend heavily on the stepdown bands and how the upfront credits are amortized. Two asks from my side before we mark this approved: 1) tighten the stepdown to tiers (0‑50% of baseline = 18% discount Y1, 50‑120% = 12% discount Y2, >120% = list price or small surcharge) — that protects margin on surge volume; 2) prefer quarterly true‑ups with carryover credits (no cash refunds) to avoid AR churn.

If you want a louder commercial incentive in year‑1 we can increase the up‑front credit but we’ll need an escalator clause that reduces credit dilution if usage falls below 60% of committed. I put a quick margin model in the spreadsheet attached.

Copying Marissa for final business approval — Marissa, can you weigh in on whether a 30% upfront credit with these stepdown tiers is okay from an account control perspective?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sr. Finance Manager, Revenue Operations
Attachment: finance_margin_model.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposal: 2yr prepay with weighted true‑up and deferred savings path

Quick note — I reviewed Ben’s points and the numbers look acceptable as a starting commercial for a strategic account. Conditional approval provided on the following terms:

- Upfront credit capped at 30% of Y1 committed value.
- Stepdown tiers as Ben recommended; include explicit language about surcharge at >120% to avoid negative margin.
- Quarterly true‑ups with credit carryover only, no refunds.
- Include a 60‑day termination right for Redwood if there is a sustained >150% usage for two consecutive quarters without fair‑use negotiation — this is a protective clause.
- SLA and performance protections required (please attach SLA_draft.pdf to the proposal).

Camila: route final proposal to Legal and Contracts (I’d suggest Alex Martinez on Contracts) and get a DocuSign envelope ready. We should also schedule a short exec alignment call with Elara to ensure procurement and engineering are aligned on the seasonal floor.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales Operations
Attachment: SLA_draft.pdf

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gonzalez <elena.gonzalez@elarahealth.com>, Mike Daniels <mike@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Final: 2yr prepay commercial and next steps

Elena / Mike —

Thanks — we’ve got conditional signoff from our finance and sales leadership on the structure below:

Summary: 2yr committed program; Y1 annualized baseline $1.2M, 30% upfront credit applied as consumption credits, stepped pricing bands for year‑2 per Ben’s model, quarterly true‑ups with carryover credits, and an SLA included. Please see the attached redline and SLA.

Next steps:
- I’ll route the redline to Contracts today (expect a Contracts review by 6/3).
- Please confirm procurement contact for DocuSign and the legal redline window (standard 3‑5 business days). We’ll open a DocuSign envelope once Contracts finishes the review: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123def
- Proposed exec alignment call: Wed 6/9 10:00 PT — confirm attendees.

If that works, I’ll queue this as a prepared SOW and we can set the billing start aligned to the DocuSign signature date.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
